newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sri Lanka confirms Nov naphtha sale to Marubeni.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka confirms Nov naphtha sale to Marubeni.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) confirmed it has awarded its November naphtha sell tender to Japanese trader, Marubeni at 62 cents a barrel below Singapore spot quotes, free-on-board (fob) Colombo, a CPC official said on Friday.
The tender for 125,000 barrels of light naphtha lifting November 28-29 which closed November 13 was valid until November 14.
Traders said the award level was very aggressive, reflective of the strong demand from North Asia for December delivery cargoes.

Tokyo naphtha prices hit their highest level in five years on November 14, with the forward open-specification contract for first-half January delivery assessed at $230/$232, surpassing the previous high of $223.50/$225.
In comparison, CPC's last naphtha cargo, 120,000 barrels lifting October 19-20, was sold at a much lower discount of $1.18 a barrel, fob Colombo.
